title: code.items batch path lacks the aggregate payload cap that code.query got
wanted_capability: The aggregate-payload invariant enforced for code.query multi-file fan-out (MAX_AGGREGATE_QUERY_CAPTURES=20000 with pre-file check, truncation flag, and files_scanned/files_total telemetry) should be mechanically generalized. The code.items({files}) batch path collects per-file payloads with no aggregate cap, so a repo-wide items sweep can still balloon the isolate heap the same way the original code.query OOM did. Wanted: an aggregate cap (shared constant or per-binding) on every multi-file collection path in the code bindings, with the same truncated/telemetry contract.
missing_primitive: aggregate payload cap on code.items batch collection
fallback_used: Callers narrow file sets manually; code.query itself is capped.
evidence: gap-fb7a1f99 (closed parent, cap landed for code.query in 947843f6)
resolution_note: obsolete: code.items batch path is now paged and aggregate-capped (MAX_ITEMS_PAGE_FILES=128, MAX_FACT_RESULT_BYTES=1 MiB, next_offset/truncated/aggregate_capped/files_scanned/files_total, per-file inventory_too_large) in 76447947, crates/bro-harness/src/bindings/code_facts.rs CodeItems::call; code.query keeps MAX_AGGREGATE_QUERY_CAPTURES; code.fields is single-file only, so no uncapped multi-file collection path remains in the code bindings.
